clue.text: At college, carry on limiting his dancing arrogantly

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university

indicators.note: the outer word sets limits round the scrambled letters, enclosing them

parts.note: to ply a trade is to carry it on

indicators.note: the letters of the word his jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: A student keeps up a haughty jig of his own while away at college.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at college is the British idiom for residing at university, Oxford or Cambridge especially.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppish is an informal adjective for self-assertive or haughty, so its adverb matches in a superior manner.

clue.text: Free relative briefly pursued by snake

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter of the relation is dropped

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A cousin gets loose for a moment before a snake gives chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursued by' means the snake comes after the shortened relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something held by a catch is to undo that fastening; both verbs mean release.

clue.text: Old man's step

definitions.meaning: pa is a father, the old man, so this is the father's possessive

explanation.surface: Father takes a step.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with an apostrophe it is father's; as a French ballet term it is a single dance step.

clue.text: Devious behaviour in some quarters creeping into work periods

indicators.note: stealing inside, so these letters go within the work periods

parts.note: shifts are spells of work
taken as written
E and S, east and south, two of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Underhand conduct is sneaking into people's working hours in certain places.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifty means evasive or untrustworthy, so the noun describes sly, deceitful conduct.

clue.text: A dessert served up: Uncle Sam's sponge

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: a fool is a creamy fruit pudding

explanation.surface: An American pudding is dished up, with a sponge cake on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a British dessert of fruit folded into cream; 'served up' reverses A FOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The bath scrubber from a gourd is spelt this way in American English, hence the nod to Uncle Sam.

clue.text: Pretentious gear demanded by educational establishment

parts.note: kit is equipment or clothing
SCH is an abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A school insists on showy uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanded by' is a link: the school comes after the gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch art is in tawdry, showy taste, aiming high and missing, so it is pretentious.

clue.text: Old Peruvian employed in Turin cathedral

indicators.note: used inside the phrase, the letters lie within the words Turin cathedral

explanation.surface: An ancient South American has a job at an Italian cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the pre-Columbian people whose empire was centred on Peru.

clue.text: Twiggy type getting rap in breakaway group

parts.note: stick is criticism, as in taking stick, a rap
taken as written
a sect is a group split from a larger body

explanation.surface: A slender model is criticised for joining a splinter faction.
explanation.walkthrough: Twiggy was a famously thin 1960s model, but here twiggy means twig-like.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is camouflaged to resemble a twig, so it is literally a twiggy creature.

clue.text: Knitted garments basket-maker kept in extremely heavy case

indicators.note: held within, so the willow goes inside the outer letters
the outer letters form a case round the willow
only the extreme letters of heavy are used

parts.note: osier is willow used in basketwork

explanation.surface: Woollens and a wicker-weaver are packed into a very heavy suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings and socks, often knitted, are sold collectively as this trade term.

clue.text: Petty infection left by small pest

indicators.note: small departs, so its letter goes from the petty word

parts.note: measly means paltry or petty
a bug is a minor infection

explanation.surface: A trifling illness is left behind by a tiny nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' is part of the wordplay, not a description of the pest.
explanation.definitionFit: This sap-sucking insect, coated in white powdery wax, damages plants and greenhouse crops.

clue.text: What one hopes for as owner of takeaway? Buy it!

definitions.text: What one hopes for as owner of takeaway?
definitions.meaning: a chip-shop owner wants money for the fried potatoes sold
to buy it is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A chip-shop owner urges a customer to make a purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to die, like the gambler exchanging tokens at the end; literally a chippy owner earns money from fries.

clue.text: Farming land includes part by river? That can be decided

indicators.note: takes in, so the farmland wraps the other letters

parts.note: arable land is ploughed for crops

indicators.note: beside, so river follows part

parts.note: a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A riverside plot within farmland raises a question for arbitration.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute open to settlement by an arbiter is one that can be resolved.

clue.text: European mayor's old staff tucking into meaty snack

indicators.note: going inside, while also suggesting eating, so the letters sit within the snack

parts.note: a burger is a meat patty in a bun
a mast is a pole or staff

explanation.surface: A continental mayor's ageing aides are tucking into hamburgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link meaning has. 'staff' suggests employees but is a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the chief magistrate of a Dutch, Flemish or German town.

clue.text: Island identified by blue cheese ultimately?

parts.note: sky blue, a colour

indicators.note: the final letter of cheese only

explanation.surface: An island famous for its blue cheese, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Dozy type intelligence chief encountered outside shelter

indicators.note: met around, so the spymaster's letters wrap round the shelter

parts.note: a spy head runs an intelligence service
lee is shelter from wind

explanation.surface: A sluggish person met the head of intelligence outside a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy person, one who is half-asleep or slow to wake, is called this affectionately.

clue.text: Standard bargain at the greengrocer's

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
a snip is a bargain

explanation.surface: A regular good deal on offer at the vegetable shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This root vegetable is a typical cheap item at a greengrocer, the whole clue picturing it.

clue.text: Awfully dull piece left unfinished — that's clear

indicators.note: badly done, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
the word piece is left without its final letter

explanation.surface: A terribly boring work is abandoned before the end, and that's plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left unfinished' trims PIECE to PIEC; 'Awfully' shuffles it with DULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellucid water or prose is transparent, translucently easy to see through or understand.

clue.text: Nonsense exclusively exposed in Times

indicators.note: shown within, so the solitary word sits inside

parts.note: by means times, as in two by three
alone means solely, exclusively

explanation.surface: Rubbish revealed only in the Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Boloney or baloney is informal American for foolish talk, humbug or rubbish.

clue.text: Young woman hiding deficiency relating to tongue

indicators.note: concealing within, so the girl's letters surround the deficiency

parts.note: gal is a girl
a loss is a shortfall

explanation.surface: A girl conceals a speech impediment of the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek glossa, this adjective is the anatomical term for things lingual.

clue.text: Info about stableman ultimately bound to cheer

indicators.note: around, so the information wraps the other letters

parts.note: gen is slang for information
a lad is a stable worker in horse racing

indicators.note: only the last letter of bound

explanation.surface: News about a groom is sure to lift the spirits in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In British racing a lad is a stable hand of any age.
explanation.definitionFit: To make glad is to lift someone's spirits, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Blokes who'd supply water heaters for some speakers

indicators.note: in some people's pronunciation the heaters' name sounds like the blokes

parts.note: in Britain a geyser is a gas water heater

explanation.surface: Chaps who would install hot water boilers, in some accents.
explanation.walkthrough: A British gas water heater is a geyser, often said 'geezer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Geezer is British slang for a man, a fellow or chap.

clue.text: Dodgy American originally performing in group touring clubs

indicators.note: placed inside the enlarged group
going round, so group surrounds clubs

parts.note: a set is a group
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: only the opening letter of performing

explanation.surface: A shady Yank first shows up playing in a band that tours nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts SET round C for SECT, and 'in' places USP within.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious or questionable is suspect, of doubtful honesty.

clue.text: Sound of friendly Cockney greeting Indian governess?

indicators.note: said aloud, the greeting matches the governess word

parts.note: the familiar hello as an East End Londoner says it, sounding like 'iya'

explanation.surface: A Londoner calls out a cheery hello.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East End Londoner, whose 'hiya' comes out as 'iya'.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India a native nursemaid or nanny was called by this word.

clue.text: Oil producer — usual type working around Cairo primarily

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the initial
functioning in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
first letter only of Cairo

explanation.surface: A typical oil business operates around Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: The gum tree yields a medicinal aromatic oil from its leaves, so it produces oil.

clue.text: Part of UK covered by a Tyneside girl

indicators.note: enclosed, so the province sits inside

parts.note: NE stands for the North East of England, where Tyneside is
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A northern girl comes from a region of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, a diminutive of Ann or Anne.

clue.text: Against one of 26's companions abandoning wine

indicators.note: leaving, so the Greek letter comes out of the wine

parts.note: Chianti is an Italian red wine
chi is another letter of the Greek alphabet, keeping company with 26

explanation.surface: One of the drinking crowd leaves the wine, being opposed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 26-down is a Greek letter, so its companions are the other Greek letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means opposed to, the same as against.

clue.text: ENT? It's where young offenders may be found

definitions.text: It's where young offenders may be found

parts.note: the three letters are the central part of the word detention

explanation.surface: An ear, nose and throat department, where young offenders turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT normally means ear, nose and throat; here it is the core of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Such institutions hold young lawbreakers or migrants in custody.

clue.text: Workers' association admitting a character in Patras

indicators.note: letting in, so the union surrounds a

parts.note: TU is a trade union

explanation.surface: A union lets in a figure from the Greek port.
explanation.walkthrough: Patras is a city in Greece, so its character is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Patras.

clue.text: Eg Scandinavian police department Reagan backed?

indicators.note: going backwards, the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department
Ron is Reagan's first name

explanation.surface: Was Reagan backed by a Scandinavian police department?
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic peoples include the Scandinavians, Finns and Icelanders, so a Swede is an example.

clue.text: Adapt again and study, like Wallace's four men

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
Edgar Wallace wrote The Four Just Men

explanation.surface: Revise and work, like the heroes of a Wallace thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify a setting again for a change is to re-adjust it.
